situation: In Sadou's compound, an old wall built many years ago is cracked. Its stones break into sandy pieces at the bottom. A new wall built last year with the same stones still looks strong.
Sadou wonders which invisible forces of nature slowly attack the old wall while the new one stays strong.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Sadou does not know which forces slowly damage the old wall.
Why is the new wall still strong?
The new wall has not yet been exposed for a long time to the sun, the rain and the air.
How can Sadou protect his walls?
He can plaster and paint them, repair cracks, keep water away from their base and remove plants that grow in the cracks.

qa.a: Weathering is the breaking down and decomposition of rocks in their place (in situ), at or near the surface of the Earth, without movement.

sum.title: I. Definition
defs: Weathering is the breaking down (disintegration) and rotting (decomposition) of rocks in their place, at or near the surface of the Earth.

qa.q: Compare the two types of weathering.
A rock breaks into pieces in the hot sun, but its minerals do not change. Which type of weathering is this?
An iron gate turns red and crumbles in the rain. Which type of weathering is similar?
qa.a: Chemical weathering: water and air react with the minerals of rocks and change them.

sum.title: II. Types of Weathering
sum.intro: There are two main types of weathering:
items: A. Physical (Mechanical) Weathering
Rocks break into smaller pieces, but their minerals do not change. Examples: thermal shattering, frost shattering, wetting and drying.
weathering_types.png
B. Chemical Weathering
Water, oxygen and acids react with the minerals of rocks and change them. The rock rots and becomes weak. Examples: solution, oxidation, carbonation, hydrolysis.

qa.q: Which type of weathering is faster in hot, dry areas, and which in hot, wet areas?
qa.a: Physical weathering is dominant in hot, dry areas. Chemical weathering is fastest in hot, wet areas, like Douala.

qa.q: Does granite weather faster or slower than limestone? Why?
qa.a: Granite weathers more slowly, because it is hard and has few cracks. Limestone is dissolved by rainwater.

qa.q: How can plants and people speed up weathering?
qa.a: Roots widen cracks and dead plants give acids. People break and expose rocks when they build roads, quarry and farm.

sum.title: III. General Factors of Weathering
sum.intro: The type and speed of weathering depend on the following factors:
items: The Factors
– Climate: hot, dry areas favour physical weathering; hot, wet areas favour chemical weathering.
– Rock characteristics: hardness, minerals and joints (cracks).
– Vegetation: roots and acids from dead plants.
– Time: the longer a rock is exposed, the more it is weathered.
– Human activities: quarrying, road building, farming and pollution.

evaluation: Weathering is the breaking down of rocks in their place, at or near the surface.
What is the difference between physical and chemical weathering?
Physical weathering breaks rocks into pieces without changing their minerals; chemical weathering changes the minerals.
Climate, rock type and vegetation (also time and human activities).
remediation: Weathering takes place in ______ (in its place).
Weathering without change of minerals is ______ weathering.
Weathering that changes minerals is ______ weathering.
Chemical weathering is fastest in hot, ______ climates.
Quarrying is a ______ factor of weathering.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. situ 2. physical 3. chemical 4. wet 5. joints 6. human
end.homework: Touch a big rock or a cement wall at 1 p.m. and again at 7 p.m. Write what you feel, and why this could break the rock after many years.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 16: Physical Weathering Processes and Products.

Correction: exfoliation is not the main physical process everywhere in Garoua; in the rainy season, chemical weathering is also very active. Both types act together.
